channel.title: CTV News – Queen's Park
channel.description: Queen's Park coverage from CTV News Toronto.

item.title: Ontario targets noisy vehicles with new steeper fines. These are the penalties drivers could face
Ontario elementary school teachers overwhelmingly vote in favour of strike mandate
item.description: The majority of members of the Elementary Teachers’ Federation of Ontario (ETFO) voted in favour of a strike action.

item.title: ‘I definitely didn’t teach him this’: Duolingo owl chirps at Doug Ford’s French
item.description: Language learning app Duolingo is clarifying that it had nothing to do with Ontario Premier Doug Ford’s tutelage after Ford’s recent comments in French drew less than complimentary reviews online.

item.title: ‘We haven’t given them any money yet’: Ontario officials hoping for good meeting with Stellantis
item.description: Ontario officials said Wednesday they’re hopeful that a meeting with the global CEO of automaker Stellantis will have a good result for the fate of some 2,200 employees who could be without jobs if a planned sale of the company’s Brampton plant goes ahead.

item.title: Ontario Premier Doug Ford touts partnerships with Quebec in Montreal speech
item.description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford says he wants to break barriers to trade between provinces and build a stronger partnership with Quebec.

item.title: Ontario secondary teachers vote 96 per cent in favour of strike mandate
item.description: Ontario public high school teachers have voted 96 per cent in favour of giving their union a strike mandate.

item.title: Ontario tables law to more quickly deal with intimate image abuse
item.description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford’s government tabled a bill Monday that would create a new legal pathway for victims of intimate image abuse to have those images deleted.

item.title: Ontario Catholic teachers vote 98 per cent in favour of strike mandate
item.description: The union representing 45,000 teachers in Ontario’s English Catholic schools says 98 per cent of its members have voted in favour of a strike mandate.

item.title: ‘We’re proud these products are from Ontario;’ Doug Ford tours Alliston, Ont. Honda plant
item.description: Premier Doug Ford is visiting Honda Canada in Alliston, Ont. on Friday.

item.title: Ontario minister suggests purpose behind meeting with Stellantis CEO is to ‘buy some time’ amid sale of Brampton plant
item.description: Officials in Ontario are hoping that an upcoming meeting with the CEO of Stellantis could help buy some time to explore options for keeping auto manufacturing jobs at a Brampton facility slated to be sold off.

item.title: Career college saw OSAP usage rise 6,000 per cent, but wasn't cut off this spring
item.description: An Ontario career college with four campuses saw the amount of students receiving financial aid explode over a few years, including an increase of nearly 6,000 per cent at one campus, but it was not one of the schools the government cut off this spring.

item.title: Premier Ford offers few words following Stellantis meeting over Brampton Assembly plant sale
item.description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford didn’t have a lot to say after a meeting with representatives of Stellantis, Unifor, and the federal government regarding the sale of the Brampton Assembly plant.

item.title: Ontario proposes OSAP changes after ‘systematic and widespread’ problems at private career colleges
item.description: The Ford government is putting forward new legislative changes that is says will strengthen oversight and accountability when it comes to OSAP student loans at private postsecondary institutions after an ongoing audit raised serious concerns about possible fraud.

item.title: Doug Ford government appoints 8 regional chairs. Here is the full list
item.description: The Ford government has named a slate of new appointed regional chairs to oversee some of the largest municipal jurisdictions in the province, including those surround Toronto.

item.title: ‘The clock is ticking:’ Ontario woman says she was denied coverage for drug to treat her rare cancer
item.description: A Toronto woman battling a rare cancer says she was “devastated” to learn that while medical professionals at Ontario’s Ministry of Health agreed she needed a potentially life-saving out-of-country treatment, bureaucrats would not sign off and didn’t inform her that her application had been recommended for approval by the ministry’s doctors.
